title: LoAS: Fully Temporal-Parallel Dataflow for Dual-Sparse Spiking Neural Networks
problem: Existing dual-sparse accelerators designed for ANNs result in sub-optimal efficiency when processing SNNs because multiple timesteps introduce an additional sequential loop, causing longer latency and increased memory traffic. The challenge is efficiently executing sparse-matrix-sparse-matrix multiplication (spMspM) across multiple temporal dimensions.
motivation: Spiking Neural Networks offer significant energy efficiency for resource-constrained edge devices, but acceleration opportunities for dual-sparse SNNs (sparse spikes and sparse weights) remain underexplored.
method: LoAS proposes a fully temporal-parallel (FTP) dataflow that treats timesteps as a parallelization dimension rather than a sequential loop, minimizing cross-timestep data movement. It introduces an FTP-friendly spike compression mechanism for efficient single-bit spike encoding with contiguous memory access, and an FTP-friendly inner-join circuit that reduces prefix-sum circuit costs while maintaining throughput.
key_novelty: The fully temporal-parallel dataflow that converts SNNs' sequential timestep dimension into a parallelizable dimension to minimize data movement and latency.
contributions: Fully temporal-parallel dataflow architecture for dual-sparse SNN acceleration
FTP-friendly spike compression mechanism enabling efficient single-bit encoding and contiguous memory access
FTP-friendly inner-join circuit reducing prefix-sum hardware costs
LoAS accelerator achieving 8.51x speedup and 3.68x energy reduction over dual-sparse baselines
primary_theme: Temporal parallelism for dual-sparse neuromorphic inference
